lead: The death toll from a suspected poisoned herbal drink in Ondo rose to 49, with about 170 people affected, and 33 suspected illegal miners died in Civil Defence custody in Niger State. Nigeria defeated a $2.35 billion arbitration claim over the Mambilla hydropower project, and a South African woman was jailed for 25 years for importing heroin. The Falconets beat England 3-0 to reach the U20 World Cup quarter-finals, and Aisha Buhari visited Atiku Abubakar.

items.h: Ondo poisoned drink death toll rises to 49
items.s: Health authorities said 49 people have now died and about 170 have been affected after drinking a suspected poisonous herbal mixture in Odigbo.

items.h: 33 suspected illegal miners die in NSCDC custody in Niger
items.s: The Civil Defence Corps ordered an investigation after 33 detained suspected illegal miners died amid a disease outbreak in its custody in Niger State.

items.h: Nigeria wins $2.35bn Mambilla arbitration
items.s: An ICC tribunal in Paris rejected Sunrise Power and Transmission's $2.35 billion claim over the stalled Mambilla hydropower project. President Tinubu said the ruling clears the way for the project.

items.h: South African woman jailed for importing heroin
items.s: The Federal High Court in Abuja handed a South African woman a long combined prison term for bringing 5.75kg of heroin into Nigeria. Reports of the total sentence differ between outlets.

items.h: Falconets beat England 3-0 to reach quarter-finals
items.s: Nigeria's under-20 women defeated England in the round of 16 of the FIFA U20 Women's World Cup in Poland on Thursday.

items.h: Aisha Buhari visits Atiku
items.s: Former First Lady Aisha Buhari, widow of the late President Muhammadu Buhari, visited ADC presidential candidate Atiku Abubakar, who announced it on social media.

items.h: Shettima clarifies remark on northern governors' support for Tinubu
items.s: The Vice President explained his earlier comment that only six northern governors backed Tinubu before he won the APC ticket.

items.h: Curfew in Mambilla after killings blamed on ethnic militia
items.s: Several people, including a security operative, were killed in the Mbamnga area of Sardauna Local Government Area, leading to a curfew.

items.h: Mutilated body of woman found in Jos forest reserve
items.s: A woman's mutilated body was discovered on Thursday morning by a stream inside the forest reserve around the Jos Wildlife Park.

items.h: Witness describes abuse of 49 abducted Orire students and teachers
items.s: A DSS witness told the Federal High Court in Abuja how pupils and teachers kidnapped from schools in Orire, Oyo State, were treated in captivity.

items.h: Troops rescue 31 kidnap victims and kill kingpin in Katsina and Kebbi
items.s: Soldiers in the North-West task force freed 31 captives and killed two terrorists, one of them a known gang leader, in separate operations in Katsina and Kebbi.

items.h: Nwabali recalled as Chelle names Super Eagles squad
items.s: Coach Eric Chelle named 24 players for the AFCON qualifiers against Madagascar and Guinea-Bissau and the friendly with Russia, with goalkeeper Stanley Nwabali returning.

items.h: NLC demands relief as petrol prices rise
items.s: The Nigeria Labour Congress asked for wage awards and naira-priced crude for local refineries to cushion higher fuel costs.

items.h: FG and unions pause King's College dispute for two weeks
items.s: The education ministry and its unions reached a five-point agreement to halt action over the proposed concession of King's College, Lagos.

items.h: Saudi Arabia rejects Nigeria's request for more Hajj slots
items.s: NAHCON said the kingdom declined to raise Nigeria's 2027 Hajj quota.

items.h: Air Peace disputes NCAA delay report
items.s: The airline said only 15 per cent of its August delays were caused by internal factors and cited discrepancies in the regulator's data.

items.h: Minister says Dangote IPO could add $60bn to NGX
items.s: A full subscription and listing would add about $60 billion to the market's capitalisation, the minister said.

items.h: FG reviews new tax laws and starts 2027 finance bill
items.s: The government began reviewing the new tax laws to fix implementation problems.

items.h: 61% of Nigerian adults in financial distress, EFInA says
items.s: The 2026 Access to Financial Services survey found most adults are under financial strain.

items.h: Gas flaring rises to 7.48%, worst since October 2025
items.s: NUPRC data showed the flaring rate jumped in August, reversing months of improvement.

items.h: APC figures split over Wike's feud with governors
items.s: South-East APC leaders backed the governors, while lawmaker Abdulmumin Jibrin and Josef Onoh urged the party to recognise Wike's role and stay united.

items.h: Obi-Kwankwaso Movement unveils 59-member campaign council
items.s: The group set up a nationwide structure covering the six zones and the FCT.

items.h: Utomi's commission to meet opposition candidates on single ticket
items.s: The Movement for Credible Elections' commission will meet shortlisted opposition candidates to push for one presidential ticket.

items.h: Major Benue governorship candidates skip peace accord
items.s: Leading candidates stayed away from a peace accord signing organised by security agencies.

items.h: Court strikes out EFCC forfeiture bid against ex-power minister Mamman
items.s: A Federal High Court in Abuja struck out the commission's motion to forfeit properties linked to Saleh Mamman.

items.h: Court upholds KC Luxury's extended detention
items.s: A Lagos Federal High Court said the NDLEA showed reasonable suspicion in the cocaine trafficking case against Afolabi Kazeem.

items.h: Former Osun council chief sues IGP for N500m
items.s: Babajide Jooda sued the Inspector-General and a former force spokesman over an arrest warrant.

items.h: Ogoni youths protest over oil production restart
items.s: Residents of Korokoro and an Ogoni youth coalition demanded inclusion and dialogue before production resumes.

items.h: ECOWAS rolls out biometric ID card
items.s: Nigeria is among seven states introducing the regional card to speed up border crossings.

items.h: Power ministry plans national complaints call centre
items.s: Minister Joseph Tegbe said Nigerians will be able to report electricity problems to a central call centre.

items.h: Phone traders reject NCC device registration fees
items.s: Mobile phone dealers asked for three to six months of public awareness before any fees are introduced.

items.h: Edo police arrest man over abuse of stepdaughter
items.s: A 57-year-old man in Auchi was arrested for allegedly defiling his six-year-old stepdaughter.

items.h: City Boy Movement inaugurates Ondo executives
items.s: The pro-Tinubu youth group launched its leadership in Akure.

items.h: Flamingos beat Niger 5-0 at WAFU B tournament
items.s: Nigeria's under-17 girls started the regional event with a big win ahead of their World Cup.

items.h: King Charles warns tech leaders about AI risks
items.s: The British monarch spoke of existential dangers if artificial intelligence falls into the wrong hands.
